future-of-interfaces.title: The Future of Human–Computer Interfaces
future-of-interfaces.excerpt: From spatial computing to neural input, we map the next decade of how we touch software — and what it means for the people who build it.

body.heading: Beyond the screen
body.text: For forty years the rectangle has been the dominant surface of computing. In this episode we sit down with three builders who think the next interface won't be a screen at all — it'll be ambient, spatial, and occasionally invisible.

We dig into the practical: what changes for product teams when input is gaze and gesture, how to design for trust when the computer is always listening, and why the most exciting hardware of 2026 is the stuff you forget you're wearing.

body.heading: What we cover
body.text: Spatial computing's real use cases, the quiet return of voice, neural input hype vs. reality, and a field guide for designers who want to start prototyping for post-screen products today.

ai-and-creativity.title: AI & the New Creative Economy
ai-and-creativity.excerpt: How generative tools are reshaping who gets to create, and how the value flows when everyone has a studio in their pocket.

body.heading: The studio in your pocket
body.text: Generative tools collapsed the distance between idea and artifact. We explore what that does to craft, to pricing, and to the careers of the people who used to own those skills.
Our guests argue that taste — not technique — is the new moat, and we pressure-test that claim with real examples from music, film, and design.

building-in-public.title: Building in Public, At Scale
building-in-public.excerpt: What happens to radical transparency when your audience is in the millions and your competitors are watching.

body.heading: Transparency as a strategy
body.text: Building in public started as a scrappy growth hack. Now it's a discipline. We talk to operators about what to share, what to hold back, and how to keep it authentic at scale.

design-systems-2026.title: Design Systems in 2026
design-systems-2026.excerpt: Where design systems are headed as AI starts generating components on demand.

body.heading: Systems that generate
body.text: If a model can produce a button, what's left for the design system? Plenty — but it changes shape. We discuss governance, tokens as the source of truth, and keeping a brand coherent when generation is cheap.

hardware-renaissance.title: The Hardware Renaissance
hardware-renaissance.excerpt: Why a new wave of founders is falling back in love with atoms, not just bits.

body.heading: Atoms are back
body.text: Cheaper prototyping, better supply chains, and AI-assisted design have made hardware founder-friendly again. We meet the people shipping physical products at software speed.

shipping-faster.title: Shipping Faster Without Burning Out
shipping-faster.excerpt: Sustainable velocity: how high-output teams protect focus and avoid the crash.

body.heading: Velocity that lasts
body.text: Speed is easy for a sprint and brutal for a year. We unpack the rituals, defaults, and boundaries that let teams stay fast without grinding their people down.
Expect concrete tactics: protected maker-time, async by default, and a healthy suspicion of the word 'urgent'.

the-mentor-mindset.title: The Mentor Mindset
the-mentor-mindset.excerpt: What separates great mentors from good ones, and how to find yours.

body.heading: The multiplier relationship
body.text: Great mentorship compounds. We talk about how to be worth mentoring, how to give feedback that lands, and why the best mentors ask more than they tell.

tools-we-love.title: Tools We Can't Live Without
tools-we-love.excerpt: Our hosts trade the apps and gadgets that actually earn a spot in the workflow.

body.heading: Earning a spot
body.text: A rapid-fire rundown of the tools that survived the test of daily use — and the over-hyped ones that didn't.

remote-by-default.title: Remote by Default
remote-by-default.excerpt: Lessons from teams that never had an office — and never missed one.

body.heading: Distance as a feature
body.text: When you design for distributed from day one, a lot of corporate theatre simply evaporates. We discuss what replaces it.

the-craft-of-listening.title: The Craft of Listening
the-craft-of-listening.excerpt: Why the best interviewers talk the least — a meta-episode on the show itself.

body.heading: The art of the pause
body.text: Silence is the interviewer's best tool. We turn the mic on ourselves and talk about preparation, presence, and knowing when to shut up.

from-idea-to-launch.title: From Idea to Launch in 30 Days
from-idea-to-launch.excerpt: A founder walks us through a real, time-boxed zero-to-one sprint.

body.heading: Constraints create momentum
body.text: A hard deadline forces real decisions. We trace one founder's 30-day path from sketch to paying customers.

designing-for-trust.title: Designing for Trust in AI Products
designing-for-trust.excerpt: Trust isn't a feature you ship — it's a hundred small decisions. Here's a framework for getting them right.

body.heading: Trust is earned in the details
body.text: Users don't read your privacy policy — they feel your product. Every loading state, every confident-but-wrong answer, every undo that isn't there: these are the moments where trust is won or lost.

body.heading: A working framework
body.text: We propose four levers: transparency (show your work), reversibility (make mistakes cheap), calibration (be confident only when you should be), and consent (no surprises). Together they turn an opaque model into a product people rely on.
None of this is about adding a 'trust' feature. It's about treating every interaction as a small promise — and keeping it.

the-quiet-power-of-defaults.title: The Quiet Power of Defaults
the-quiet-power-of-defaults.excerpt: Most users never change a setting. That makes your defaults the most important design decision you'll make.

body.heading: The path of least resistance
body.text: Defaults are decisions you make on behalf of everyone who won't decide for themselves — which is almost everyone. Choose them with the weight they deserve.

writing-as-thinking.title: Writing Is Thinking
writing-as-thinking.excerpt: If you can't write it clearly, you don't understand it yet. A case for the document as a thinking tool.

body.heading: Prose as a forcing function
body.text: Slides let you hide gaps. Prose exposes them. Writing the doc is how you find out whether the idea actually holds together.

small-teams-big-leverage.title: Small Teams, Big Leverage
small-teams-big-leverage.excerpt: Why the most productive teams of 2026 are smaller than ever — and what that demands of each person.

body.heading: Leverage over headcount
body.text: Tooling has raised the ceiling on what a single motivated person can do. The constraint is no longer hands — it's coordination. Small teams win by needing less of it.

the-interface-is-the-product.title: The Interface Is the Product
the-interface-is-the-product.excerpt: Your backend is invisible. The interface is the entire experience your users will ever have.

body.heading: Users meet the surface
body.text: No one experiences your architecture. They experience the surface you put in front of them. Invest accordingly.
